topics.title: Introduction to Spring Boot
topics.content:

Introduction to Spring Boot

Beginner ⏱️ 8 min read Updated: September 2026

Spring Boot is an open-source Java-based framework used to create a microservice. It is developed by Pivotal Team and is used to build stand-alone and production-ready spring applications. This chapter will introduce you to Spring Boot and familiarize you with its basic concepts.

The Spring framework has become the de facto standard for enterprise Java development. However, setting up a Spring application used to involve a tremendous amount of configuration, including XML files or extensive Java configuration classes, configuring servers, and setting up dependency management. Spring Boot changes all of that. It takes an opinionated view of the Spring platform and third-party libraries so you can get started with minimum fuss. Most Spring Boot applications need minimal Spring configuration.

The primary goals of Spring Boot are:

  • To provide a radically faster and widely accessible getting-started experience for all Spring development.
  • To be opinionated out of the box but get out of the way quickly as requirements start to diverge from the defaults.
  • To provide a range of non-functional features that are common to large classes of projects (such as embedded servers, security, metrics, health checks, and externalized configuration).
  • Absolutely no code generation and no requirement for XML configuration.

topics.title: Spring vs Spring Boot
topics.content:
Tutorials > Backend > Spring Boot > Basics

Spring vs Spring Boot

Concept ⏱️ 8 min read Updated: September 2026

While Spring and Spring Boot are related, they serve different purposes. The Spring Framework provides a comprehensive programming and configuration model for modern Java-based enterprise applications - on any kind of deployment platform. A key element of Spring is infrastructural support at the application level: Spring focuses on the "plumbing" of enterprise applications so that teams can focus on application-level business logic, without unnecessary ties to specific deployment environments.

On the other hand, Spring Boot is essentially an extension of the Spring framework which eliminated the boilerplate configurations required for setting up a Spring application.

Key Differences:

  • Configuration: Spring Framework requires explicit configuration using XML or Java annotations. Spring Boot introduces the concept of auto-configuration, which automatically configures the application based on the dependencies present in the classpath.
  • Servers: In a standard Spring application, you have to build a WAR file and deploy it into a standalone web server like Tomcat, WebSphere, or Weblogic. Spring Boot provides an embedded server (like Tomcat, Jetty, or Undertow), allowing you to package your application as a standalone executable JAR.
  • Dependency Management: Spring requires you to individually define dependencies and their compatible versions. Spring Boot uses "Starter POMs" that group related dependencies together, significantly simplifying the Maven or Gradle build files and reducing version conflicts.

topics.title: Architecture of Spring Boot
topics.content:
Tutorials > Backend > Spring Boot > Basics

Architecture of Spring Boot

Architecture ⏱️ 10 min read Updated: September 2026

Spring Boot’s architecture is built on top of the Spring framework, meaning it utilizes all of Spring's features while abstracting the complexities of configuration. The architecture consists of several layers:

  1. Presentation Layer: This is the topmost layer where the user interface or API endpoints reside. It handles HTTP requests, translates JSON parameters to objects, authenticates the request, and transfers it to the business layer.
  2. Business Layer: This layer contains the core business logic. It handles all the business rules, validations, and data processing. It receives requests from the presentation layer, performs operations, and may fetch data from the data access layer.
  3. Persistence Layer: This layer is responsible for database interactions. It translates business objects into database rows and vice-versa. Technologies like Spring Data JPA or Hibernate are typically used here.
  4. Database Layer: The actual database where data is stored (e.g., MySQL, PostgreSQL, MongoDB).

Spring Boot sits above these layers, providing an execution environment (via embedded Tomcat), automatic configuration of these layers (like automatically configuring a DataSource if a database driver is detected), and starter dependencies to easily pull in the necessary libraries for each layer.

topics.title: Environment Setup
topics.content:
Tutorials > Backend > Spring Boot > Basics

Environment Setup

Setup ⏱️ 12 min read Updated: September 2026

Setting up a Spring Boot environment is straightforward. You will need a few essential tools:

  • Java Development Kit (JDK): Spring Boot applications are written in Java, so you need the JDK. Java 17 or Java 21 are the recommended versions for modern Spring Boot 3.x development.
  • Build Tool: Maven or Gradle are used to manage dependencies and build the project. Maven uses an pom.xml file, while Gradle uses a build.gradle file.
  • IDE: An Integrated Development Environment (IDE) like IntelliJ IDEA, Eclipse, or Visual Studio Code (with Java extensions) is essential for a productive development experience.

Dependencies (Starter, BOM, Spring Parent):

When using Maven, a typical Spring Boot project inherits from the spring-boot-starter-parent. This parent POM provides default configurations, Java version settings, and plugin configurations. More importantly, it brings in a Dependency Management section (often called a BOM - Bill of Materials) that dictates the compatible versions of all Spring and third-party libraries. This means you only declare the dependency (like spring-boot-starter-web) without specifying a version, and the parent POM ensures you get the correct, compatible version.

"Starters" are a set of convenient dependency descriptors you can include in your application. For example, if you want to build a web application, you simply add the spring-boot-starter-web dependency, which transitively pulls in Spring MVC, Jackson (for JSON), Tomcat, and other necessary libraries.

topics.title: Application Properties
topics.content:
Tutorials > Backend > Spring Boot > Basics

Application Properties

Configuration ⏱️ 10 min read Updated: September 2026

Spring Boot allows you to externalize your configuration so that you can work with the same application code in different environments (dev, test, prod). You can use properties files, YAML files, environment variables, and command-line arguments to externalize configuration.

The most common file used for configuration is application.properties or application.yml, located in the src/main/resources directory.

By default, Spring Boot runs a web application on port 8080. You can easily change this by adding a single line to application.properties:

PROPERTIES Code Snippet
server.port=9090
spring.application.name=my-app

You can also define custom properties and inject them into your Spring Beans using the @Value annotation or by binding them to structured objects using @ConfigurationProperties. This externalized configuration is a powerful feature that makes Spring Boot applications highly adaptable to cloud environments and containerized deployments where configuration often changes between stages.

topics.title: Annotations
topics.content:
Tutorials > Backend > Spring Boot > Core

Annotations

Core Concept ⏱️ 10 min read Updated: September 2026

Annotations in Spring Boot are a form of metadata that provide data about a program but are not part of the program itself. They dictate how the Spring Framework should configure the application context and manage beans. The most critical annotation in a Spring Boot application is @SpringBootApplication.

@SpringBootApplication is a convenience annotation that combines three essential annotations:

  • @EnableAutoConfiguration: Enables Spring Boot's auto-configuration mechanism.
  • @ComponentScan: Enables @Component scan on the package where the application is located. It tells Spring to look for other components, configurations, and services in the specified package and its sub-packages.
  • @Configuration: Allows to register extra beans in the context or import additional configuration classes.

Other widely used annotations include @Component (a generic stereotype for any Spring-managed component), @Service (specialization of @Component for service layer classes), @Repository (for Data Access Objects), and @Controller (for presentation layer classes). These annotations help Spring identify and register beans in the Application Context.

topics.title: Auto-configuration
topics.content:
Tutorials > Backend > Spring Boot > Core

Auto-configuration

Magic ⏱️ 12 min read Updated: September 2026

Auto-configuration is perhaps the most magical and powerful feature of Spring Boot. It attempts to automatically configure your Spring application based on the jar dependencies that you have added. For example, if HSQLDB is on your classpath, and you have not manually configured any database connection beans, then Spring Boot auto-configures an in-memory database.

Spring Boot analyzes the classpath, existing beans, and various property settings to deduce what the developer intends to configure. If it finds the spring-webmvc jar, it configures a DispatcherServlet, default error pages, and embedded Tomcat.

This behavior is driven by @Conditional annotations. Auto-configuration classes use conditions like @ConditionalOnClass, @ConditionalOnMissingBean, and @ConditionalOnProperty to decide whether a configuration should be applied. For instance, an auto-configuration might say: "If the class DataSource is present, and if the user hasn't defined their own DataSource bean, then configure a default one." This allows developers to easily override auto-configuration by simply defining their own beans.

topics.title: Dependency Injection
topics.content:
Tutorials > Backend > Spring Boot > Core

Dependency Injection

Design Pattern ⏱️ 14 min read Updated: September 2026

Dependency Injection (DI) is a core concept of the Spring Framework. It is a design pattern that implements Inversion of Control for resolving dependencies. In traditional programming, if Class A needs Class B, Class A will instantiate Class B using the new keyword. With DI, the framework creates Class B and injects it into Class A. This promotes loose coupling and makes testing significantly easier.

There are primarily three types of Dependency Injection in Spring:

  1. Constructor Injection: The dependencies are provided through a class constructor. This is the recommended approach because it ensures that the bean is initialized in a valid state (all mandatory dependencies are satisfied) and allows the fields to be marked as final.
  2. Setter Injection: The dependencies are injected using setter methods. This is useful for optional dependencies that can be changed or re-injected later.
  3. Field Injection: Dependencies are injected directly into the fields using the @Autowired annotation. While concise, this is generally discouraged as it makes the class tightly coupled to the Spring container and harder to unit test without reflection.

topics.title: Inversion of Control (IoC)
topics.content:
Tutorials > Backend > Spring Boot > Core

Inversion of Control (IoC)

Design Pattern ⏱️ 10 min read Updated: September 2026

Inversion of Control (IoC) is a programming principle where the control flow of a program is inverted compared to traditional procedural programming. In the context of Spring, IoC means that objects do not create other objects on which they rely to do their work. Instead, they get the objects that they need from an outside source (the Spring IoC Container).

The Spring IoC container is responsible for instantiating, configuring, and assembling beans. The container gets its instructions on what objects to instantiate, configure, and assemble by reading configuration metadata. The configuration metadata is represented in XML, Java annotations, or Java code.

The IoC container manages the lifecycle of the objects it creates. By delegating the responsibility of object creation and dependency resolution to the framework, developers can write code that is modular, decoupled, and focused purely on business logic rather than boilerplate wiring.

topics.title: Spring Bean Lifecycle
topics.content:
Tutorials > Backend > Spring Boot > Core

Spring Bean Lifecycle

Deep Dive ⏱️ 12 min read Updated: September 2026

A Spring Bean is simply an object that is instantiated, assembled, and managed by a Spring IoC container. Understanding the lifecycle of a Spring Bean is crucial for performing custom initialization or destruction logic.

The lifecycle consists of several phases:

  1. Instantiation: The Spring container instantiates the bean using its constructor.
  2. Populate Properties: Spring injects the necessary dependencies (DI) based on configuration.
  3. Aware Interfaces: If the bean implements interfaces like BeanNameAware or ApplicationContextAware, the container calls their respective methods.
  4. Pre-initialization: The postProcessBeforeInitialization method of any configured BeanPostProcessors is called.
  5. Initialization: Custom initialization methods are called (e.g., methods annotated with @PostConstruct or the afterPropertiesSet method of InitializingBean).
  6. Post-initialization: The postProcessAfterInitialization method of any configured BeanPostProcessors is called. The bean is now ready for use.
  7. Destruction: When the application context is closed, the bean is destroyed. Methods annotated with @PreDestroy or the destroy method of DisposableBean are executed, allowing for resource cleanup.

topics.title: Connecting to MySQL
topics.content:
Tutorials > Backend > Spring Boot > Database

Connecting to MySQL

Integration ⏱️ 10 min read Updated: September 2026

Most enterprise applications need to store and retrieve data from a relational database. Spring Boot makes connecting to databases like MySQL incredibly simple through auto-configuration. To connect to MySQL, you need to add two primary dependencies to your pom.xml: the Spring Data JPA starter (spring-boot-starter-data-jpa) and the MySQL JDBC driver (mysql-connector-j).

Once the dependencies are in place, you only need to provide the connection details in your application.properties or application.yml file:

PROPERTIES Code Snippet
spring.datasource.url=jdbc:mysql://localhost:3306/mydb
spring.datasource.username=root
spring.datasource.password=secret
spring.datasource.driver-class-name=com.mysql.cj.jdbc.Driver

# JPA/Hibernate properties
spring.jpa.hibernate.ddl-auto=update
spring.jpa.show-sql=true

Spring Boot's auto-configuration detects these properties and automatically configures a DataSource, an EntityManagerFactory, and a TransactionManager. The ddl-auto=update property tells Hibernate to automatically update the database schema based on your entity classes, which is very useful during development.

topics.title: Entity, Repository, CRUD
topics.content:
Tutorials > Backend > Spring Boot > Database

Entity, Repository, CRUD

Data Access ⏱️ 15 min read Updated: September 2026

In Spring Data JPA, data models are represented by Entities. An Entity is a simple Java POJO annotated with @Entity, mapping it to a database table. The @Id annotation specifies the primary key, and @GeneratedValue dictates how the ID is generated.

JAVA Code Snippet
@Entity
public class User {
    @Id
    @GeneratedValue(strategy = GenerationType.IDENTITY)
    private Long id;
    private String name;
    private String email;
    // Getters and setters
}

To interact with the database, you create a Repository interface that extends JpaRepository.

JAVA Code Snippet
public interface UserRepository extends JpaRepository<User, Long> {
}

By simply extending this interface, Spring Data JPA automatically provides implementations for common CRUD (Create, Read, Update, Delete) operations. You don't need to write any SQL or boilerplate data access code. You can instantly use methods like save(), findById(), findAll(), and deleteById() in your service layer to manage data.

topics.title: JDBC vs Spring Data JPA
topics.content:
Tutorials > Backend > Spring Boot > Database

JDBC vs Spring Data JPA

Comparison ⏱️ 8 min read Updated: September 2026

Java Database Connectivity (JDBC) is the standard Java API for connecting to databases. While powerful, using raw JDBC requires writing a lot of boilerplate code: opening connections, creating statements, executing queries, iterating over result sets, handling exceptions, and closing resources. This process is error-prone and tedious.

Spring Data JPA is built on top of the Java Persistence API (JPA) and Hibernate. It abstracts away the complexities of JDBC and provides a highly productive repository-based approach to data access.

Key differences:

  • Abstraction Level: JDBC is a low-level API dealing with SQL strings and result sets. JPA deals with Java objects (Entities) and object-relational mapping (ORM).
  • Productivity: Spring Data JPA drastically reduces boilerplate code. You declare an interface, and the framework generates the implementation. With JDBC, you write everything manually.
  • Database Independence: JPA uses JPQL (Java Persistence Query Language), which is database agnostic. JDBC relies on database-specific SQL syntax. While JPA is generally preferred for standard CRUD and complex domain models, JDBC (or Spring's JdbcTemplate) might still be used for highly optimized, complex SQL queries where ORM overhead is a concern.

topics.title: Custom Queries in JPA
topics.content:
Tutorials > Backend > Spring Boot > Database

Custom Queries in JPA

Advanced ⏱️ 12 min read Updated: September 2026

While JpaRepository provides standard CRUD operations, you often need to fetch data based on specific criteria. Spring Data JPA offers several ways to define custom queries without writing implementations.

1. Query Methods (Derived Queries):

You can define queries simply by naming your interface methods according to specific conventions. Spring Data parses the method name and generates the SQL.

JAVA Code Snippet
List<User> findByEmail(String email);
List<User> findByNameContaining(String name);

2. @Query Annotation:

For more complex queries that cannot be easily expressed via method names, you can use the @Query annotation to write JPQL (or native SQL) directly on the repository method.

JAVA Code Snippet
@Query("SELECT u FROM User u WHERE u.status = 'ACTIVE' AND u.age > :age")
List<User> findActiveUsersOlderThan(@Param("age") int age);

// Native SQL
@Query(value = "SELECT * FROM users WHERE email_verified = true", nativeQuery = true)
List<User> findVerifiedUsers();

This flexibility allows developers to handle complex data retrieval scenarios efficiently while staying within the Spring Data ecosystem.

topics.title: Introduction to REST APIs
topics.content:
Tutorials > Backend > Spring Boot > REST

Introduction to REST APIs

API Design ⏱️ 8 min read Updated: September 2026

REST (Representational State Transfer) is an architectural style for designing networked applications. It relies on a stateless, client-server, cacheable communications protocol — almost always HTTP. RESTful applications use HTTP requests to post data (create and/or update), read data (e.g., make queries), and delete data.

In a REST architecture, the focus is on resources, which are identified by URIs (Uniform Resource Identifiers). The client interacts with these resources using standard HTTP methods:

  • GET: Retrieve a resource.
  • POST: Create a new resource.
  • PUT: Update an existing resource entirely.
  • PATCH: Update an existing resource partially.
  • DELETE: Remove a resource.

Spring Boot is an excellent framework for building RESTful web services. It provides a robust set of annotations and tools out of the box (via spring-boot-starter-web) that handle request routing, parameter binding, and JSON serialization, allowing developers to focus on defining the API's behavior.

topics.title: @RestController & @RequestMapping
topics.content:
Tutorials > Backend > Spring Boot > REST

@RestController & @RequestMapping

Core Web ⏱️ 12 min read Updated: September 2026

In Spring MVC, a controller is a class responsible for handling incoming HTTP requests. The @RestController annotation is a specialized version of the standard @Controller annotation. It is a convenience annotation that combines @Controller and @ResponseBody.

When a class is annotated with @RestController, Spring knows that the methods within this class will return data (typically JSON or XML) directly to the client, rather than returning a view name (like an HTML template). Every request handling method of the controller class automatically serializes return objects into HttpResponse.

The @RequestMapping annotation is used to map web requests to specific handler classes and/or handler methods. It can be applied at the class level to define a base URI for all endpoints within the controller.

JAVA Code Snippet
@RestController
@RequestMapping("/api/users")
public class UserController {
    // All endpoints here will be prefixed with /api/users
}

topics.title: Handling HTTP Methods
topics.content:
Tutorials > Backend > Spring Boot > REST

Handling HTTP Methods

Routing ⏱️ 10 min read Updated: September 2026

Spring provides specialized, method-level annotations for mapping specific HTTP request methods to controller methods. These are shorthand for @RequestMapping(method = RequestMethod.GET) and so on, making the code more readable and expressive.

  • @GetMapping: Maps HTTP GET requests. Used to fetch data.
JAVA Code Snippet
  @GetMapping
  public List<User> getAllUsers() { ... }
  • @PostMapping: Maps HTTP POST requests. Used to create new resources.
JAVA Code Snippet
  @PostMapping
  public User createUser(...) { ... }
  • @PutMapping: Maps HTTP PUT requests. Used to update an entire resource.
JAVA Code Snippet
  @PutMapping("/{id}")
  public User updateUser(...) { ... }
  • @DeleteMapping: Maps HTTP DELETE requests. Used to delete a resource.
JAVA Code Snippet
  @DeleteMapping("/{id}")
  public void deleteUser(...) { ... }

topics.title: Data Binding
topics.content:
Tutorials > Backend > Spring Boot > REST

Data Binding

Request Handling ⏱️ 12 min read Updated: September 2026

To process requests, your API often needs data sent by the client. Spring provides annotations to easily extract this data from various parts of the HTTP request.

  • @PathVariable: Extracts values from the URI path. For example, in /api/users/123, 123 is a path variable.
JAVA Code Snippet
  @GetMapping("/{userId}")
  public User getUserById(@PathVariable Long userId) { ... }
  • @RequestParam: Extracts query parameters from the URI. For example, in /api/users?status=active, status is a request param.
JAVA Code Snippet
  @GetMapping("/search")
  public List<User> searchUsers(@RequestParam String status) { ... }
  • @RequestBody: Maps the body of the HTTP request to a Java object. This is crucial for POST and PUT requests where the client sends a JSON payload. Spring automatically uses a message converter (like Jackson) to deserialize the JSON into the specified Java type.
JAVA Code Snippet
  @PostMapping
  public User createUser(@RequestBody User newUser) { ... }

topics.title: JSON Serialization/Deserialization
topics.content:
Tutorials > Backend > Spring Boot > REST

JSON Serialization/Deserialization

Data Conversion ⏱️ 10 min read Updated: September 2026

When building REST APIs with Spring Boot, data exchange is predominantly done using JSON. Spring Boot relies heavily on the Jackson library for processing JSON data. Jackson is automatically configured when you include the spring-boot-starter-web dependency.

  • Serialization: The process of converting a Java object into a JSON string to send it in the HTTP response. When a @RestController method returns an object, Jackson automatically serializes it to JSON.
  • Deserialization: The process of converting a JSON string from an HTTP request body into a Java object. This happens automatically when you use the @RequestBody annotation.

You can customize Jackson's behavior using annotations on your data models. For example, @JsonIgnore prevents a field (like a password) from being serialized into the JSON response. @JsonProperty("custom_name") changes the key name used in the JSON output, differing from the Java field name. @JsonFormat can be used to dictate how dates and times are formatted in the JSON payload.

topics.title: Quiz

quiz.question: Which three core annotations are composed into the meta-annotation '@SpringBootApplication'?
quiz.explanation: @SpringBootApplication encapsulates @Configuration (declares class as a source of bean definitions), @EnableAutoConfiguration (guesses and configures beans based on classpath dependencies), and @ComponentScan (scans the current package and sub-packages for Spring components).

quiz.question: What is the default bean scope in the Spring IoC Container?
quiz.explanation: In Spring, beans are 'singleton' by default. Exactly one shared instance is instantiated and retained in the ApplicationContext cache per bean definition.

quiz.question: What is the primary difference between '@Controller' and '@RestController' in Spring MVC?
options: @RestController is only used for microservices with Eureka
@RestController is a convenience meta-annotation that combines @Controller and @ResponseBody, serializing returned objects directly into HTTP response bodies (JSON/XML)
@Controller returns JSON while @RestController returns JSP views
quiz.explanation: @RestController = @Controller + @ResponseBody. Every handler method in a @RestController automatically serializes domain return values into JSON/XML responses using Jackson, instead of resolving HTML view templates.

quiz.question: Why is Constructor Injection strongly recommended over Field Injection (@Autowired on private fields)?
options: Constructor injection enables fields to be declared 'final' (immutable), ensures beans cannot be initialized with null dependencies, and allows easy unit testing with mocks without reflection
Constructor injection is faster to compile
Field injection was removed in Spring 5
quiz.explanation: Constructor injection guarantees total immutability (final fields), prevents partial bean instantiation, avoids hidden circular dependencies, and enables clean POJO unit testing without needing Spring reflection containers.

quiz.question: How does Spring Boot Auto-Configuration know which beans to configure?
options: It reads all XML files in the OS file system
It evaluates conditional annotations like @ConditionalOnClass, @ConditionalOnMissingBean, and @ConditionalOnProperty listed in auto-configuration import files
It queries the database schema at compile time
quiz.explanation: Auto-configuration scans candidate classes in META-INF/spring/...AutoConfiguration.imports and evaluates condition annotations (e.g. configuring a DataSource only if DataSource.class is on classpath and no custom DataSource bean exists).

quiz.question: Which Spring Boot Starter dependency is required to build RESTful web services using Apache Tomcat and Spring MVC?
quiz.explanation: 'spring-boot-starter-web' bundles Spring MVC, REST support, Jackson JSON serialization, and embedded Apache Tomcat as the default servlet container.

quiz.question: What is the function of Spring Boot Actuator?
options: Compiles Java code to native GraalVM images
Provides production-ready observability endpoints such as health checks (/actuator/health), metrics, thread dumps, and audit logs
quiz.explanation: Spring Boot Actuator brings production monitoring and management capabilities, exposing HTTP/JMX endpoints for health probes (vital for Kubernetes liveness/readiness), JVM metrics, and application info.

quiz.question: What is the N+1 select problem in Spring Data JPA / Hibernate?
options: An issue where fetching N parent records with lazy/eager associations triggers 1 query for the parents and N subsequent individual SQL queries for each parent's children
A limitation preventing tables from having more than N columns
quiz.explanation: The N+1 problem occurs when fetching a list of parent entities (1 query) causes Hibernate to fire a separate SQL query for each individual parent's relationship (N queries), severely degrading database performance.

quiz.question: How do you solve the N+1 problem using JPQL in a Spring Data repository?
options: Use 'JOIN FETCH' in the JPQL query (e.g. 'SELECT p FROM Post p JOIN FETCH p.comments')
quiz.explanation: 'JOIN FETCH' instructs Hibernate to perform an inner or left outer join in SQL, loading the parent and all associated child entities simultaneously in a single database query.

quiz.question: What is the effect of applying '@Transactional' on a service class method in Spring?
options: Wraps method execution within a database transaction via an AOP proxy, committing on success and rolling back on RuntimeException or Error
Converts the method into an asynchronous task
quiz.explanation: Spring AOP intercepts the method call, opens a database transaction, invokes the target logic, and commits if no unhandled RuntimeException occurs. By default, checked exceptions do NOT trigger a rollback unless rollbackFor is specified.

quiz.question: Why does calling a '@Transactional' method from another method WITHIN THE SAME CLASS fail to start a transaction (self-invocation problem)?
options: Transactions are prohibited on private methods
Spring's proxy-based AOP architecture intercepts calls entering through the proxy; direct internal method calls bypass the proxy entirely
Internal calls cause JVM stack overflow
The database blocks nested method calls
quiz.explanation: Spring manages transactions via dynamic CGLIB/JDK proxies. In a self-invocation (this.method()), the call is dispatched directly on the raw target object, completely bypassing the transaction interceptor proxy.

quiz.question: Which Transaction Propagation setting ensures a new, independent transaction is always created, suspending any existing transaction?
quiz.explanation: Propagation.REQUIRES_NEW suspends any current outer transaction and creates an entirely new independent physical transaction with its own commit/rollback boundaries.

quiz.question: What annotation is used to create global, centralized exception handling across all @RequestMapping controllers?
quiz.explanation: @ControllerAdvice (and @RestControllerAdvice) uses AOP to intercept exceptions thrown by any controller method, handling them with centralized @ExceptionHandler methods.

quiz.question: What is the difference between '@RequestParam' and '@PathVariable'?
options: '@PathVariable' extracts values directly from the URI path segment (e.g. /users/{id}); '@RequestParam' extracts query parameters from the URL query string (e.g. /users?id=123)
'@RequestParam' is only used for POST bodies
quiz.explanation: @PathVariable binds placeholder URI path segments (/api/orders/{id}). @RequestParam binds URL query parameters (/api/orders?status=active) or form data fields.

quiz.question: Which annotation binds the HTTP request body JSON directly into a Java domain object via Jackson serialization?
quiz.explanation: @RequestBody signals Spring to deserialize the incoming HTTP request body (JSON/XML) into the method parameter object using an HttpMessageConverter (such as Jackson).

quiz.question: What annotation is used to bind external configuration properties from application.properties to a strongly-typed Java class?
quiz.explanation: @ConfigurationProperties(prefix = 'app.security') provides hierarchical, type-safe binding of configuration properties into bean fields with support for validation and IDE auto-completion.

quiz.question: How does the '@Profile("production")' annotation control bean instantiation?
options: Ensures the annotated component or configuration bean is only registered in the ApplicationContext when the 'production' profile is active (spring.profiles.active=production)
Restricts access to admin users only
quiz.explanation: @Profile conditionally activates or deactivates beans, configurations, and properties based on active environment profiles (e.g. dev, test, prod).

quiz.question: What is the role of the DispatcherServlet in Spring Boot MVC?
options: It connects to the database via JDBC
It acts as the Front Controller, intercepting all incoming HTTP requests and dispatching them to the appropriate HandlerMapping, Controller, and ViewResolver
It manages Tomcat thread pool threads
quiz.explanation: The DispatcherServlet implements the Front Controller pattern, serving as the single entry point for all HTTP requests to route them through interceptors, controllers, and message converters.

quiz.question: Which method in a Spring Bean implements post-initialization logic immediately after all bean properties and dependencies have been injected?
options: A method annotated with @PostConstruct (or implementing InitializingBean)
quiz.explanation: The @PostConstruct annotation designates a method to be executed immediately after dependency injection is complete and before the bean is made available to callers.

quiz.question: What is the difference between CrudRepository and JpaRepository in Spring Data?
options: JpaRepository extends PagingAndSortingRepository and CrudRepository, adding JPA-specific features like flush(), saveAndFlush(), batch deletions, and pagination/sorting support
CrudRepository only works with NoSQL databases
JpaRepository does not support CRUD operations
quiz.explanation: JpaRepository inherits CRUD and pagination/sorting capabilities from CrudRepository and PagingAndSortingRepository, adding flush() persistence context operations and deleteInBatch().

quiz.question: What does the 'mappedBy' attribute signify on a bidirectional JPA relationship (e.g. @OneToMany(mappedBy = 'author'))?
options: It maps the table name in the database
It identifies that the current entity is the inverse (non-owning) side of the relationship, pointing to the owning field on the target entity that manages the foreign key column
It creates an index on the author column
quiz.explanation: 'mappedBy' designates the inverse relationship side. The side WITHOUT mappedBy is the owning side that physically holds and manages the foreign key column in SQL.

quiz.question: Which Hibernate cascade type causes child entities to be automatically removed from the database when removed from the parent entity's collection?
quiz.explanation: Setting 'orphanRemoval = true' instructs Hibernate to automatically delete child records from the database when they are dereferenced or removed from the parent's collection.

quiz.question: What is the purpose of the '@Valid' or '@Validated' annotation on a request body parameter?
options: Checks that the user is logged in
Triggers Bean Validation (Hibernate Validator) on the incoming object according to JSR-380 constraints (@NotNull, @NotBlank, @Min, @Email)
quiz.explanation: @Valid activates Jakarta Bean Validation. If any constraint on the payload fails, a MethodArgumentNotValidException is thrown with detailed field error results.

quiz.question: What is the difference between '@NotNull', '@NotEmpty', and '@NotBlank' in Bean Validation?
options: @NotNull checks value != null; @NotEmpty checks not null and length/size > 0; @NotBlank checks not null, not empty, and contains at least one non-whitespace character (strings only)
@NotBlank can be used on lists and numbers
quiz.explanation: @NotNull rejects null. @NotEmpty rejects null and empty collections/strings (""). @NotBlank rejects null, empty, and strings containing only whitespace characters ("   ").

quiz.question: What HTTP status code is represented by 'HttpStatus.CREATED'?
quiz.explanation: HTTP 201 Created indicates that the request succeeded and resulted in the successful creation of a new resource (standard response for POST creation endpoints).

quiz.question: What HTTP status code is represented by 'HttpStatus.NO_CONTENT'?
quiz.explanation: HTTP 204 No Content indicates that the action succeeded and no response body payload is returned (commonly returned for successful DELETE operations).

quiz.question: What is the purpose of the '@Modifying' annotation in Spring Data JPA?
options: Permits modifying table schema at runtime
Informs Spring Data JPA that the query is an UPDATE or DELETE DML statement rather than a SELECT query
Enables dirty checking on returned entities
Forces query execution in a separate thread
quiz.explanation: @Modifying is required on custom @Query methods that execute DML (UPDATE, DELETE, INSERT) operations, instructing the EntityManager to execute executeUpdate() instead of executeQuery().

quiz.question: What is the primary role of the SecurityFilterChain bean in modern Spring Security 6+?
options: Defines the chain of security filter rules, URL authorization matchers, CSRF settings, session management, and authentication providers for HTTP requests
quiz.explanation: In Spring Security 5.7+ / 6+, WebSecurityConfigurerAdapter is deprecated. Developers configure a SecurityFilterChain @Bean to declare authorizeHttpRequests, OAuth2, and filters.

quiz.question: Why should passwords never be stored using simple hash algorithms like MD5 or SHA-256 in Spring applications?
options: Spring Security does not support MD5
They are fast computation algorithms vulnerable to brute-force and precomputed rainbow table attacks; salted adaptive key-stretching algorithms like BCrypt or Argon2 must be used
MD5 hashes are too long for database columns
quiz.explanation: MD5 and SHA-256 can compute billions of hashes per second on modern GPUs. BCrypt includes a configurable work factor and automatic salting to deliberately slow down brute-force attacks.

quiz.question: What does the '@Async' annotation do when applied to a method?
options: Runs the method in a separate background thread allocated from a ThreadPoolTaskExecutor, returning immediately to the caller (often returning CompletableFuture<T>)
Blocks the calling thread until completed
Executes the method on a web browser client
quiz.explanation: @Async (coupled with @EnableAsync on configuration) executes the annotated method asynchronously in a background thread pool, allowing non-blocking execution for long tasks like email dispatch.

quiz.question: What does the '@Scheduled' annotation accomplish in Spring Boot?
options: Executes a method periodically at fixed intervals or based on a cron expression (requires @EnableScheduling)
quiz.explanation: @Scheduled configures recurring background tasks using fixedRate, fixedDelay, or cron expressions when @EnableScheduling is active.

quiz.question: What is the difference between 'fixedRate' and 'fixedDelay' in @Scheduled tasks?
options: 'fixedRate' measures time between the START of successive invocations; 'fixedDelay' measures time between the FINISH of one invocation and the start of the next
quiz.explanation: 'fixedRate' starts tasks every N milliseconds regardless of execution time. 'fixedDelay' guarantees N milliseconds of idle time AFTER the preceding execution finishes.

quiz.question: What is the purpose of the '@MockBean' (or '@MockitoBean' in Spring Boot 3.4+) annotation in tests?
options: Adds a Mockito mock of the bean into the Spring ApplicationContext, replacing any existing real bean of that type for integration testing
quiz.explanation: @MockBean registers a Mockito mock inside the Spring ApplicationContext, allowing isolated testing of controllers (@WebMvcTest) with mocked service dependencies.

quiz.question: What test annotation is used to test ONLY the web layer (controllers, validation, JSON serialization) without loading the full database/service context?
quiz.explanation: @WebMvcTest focuses strictly on Spring MVC components (@Controller, @RestController, Converter), skipping @Service and @Repository beans to ensure rapid execution.

quiz.question: What is the purpose of '@DataJpaTest'?
options: Configures an in-memory database, scans @Entity classes, and configures Spring Data JPA repositories within a transactional rollback test environment
quiz.explanation: @DataJpaTest focuses solely on JPA components, using an embedded in-memory database (like H2) by default and rolling back transactions at the end of each test.

quiz.question: What does the 'server.servlet.context-path' property in application.properties do?
options: Configures the local file system path for file uploads
Sets the prefix path for all HTTP endpoints exposed by the embedded servlet container (e.g. localhost:8080/api/v1/...)
quiz.explanation: Setting 'server.servlet.context-path=/api/v1' prefixes all web application endpoints with '/api/v1' across the entire application.

quiz.question: What is the purpose of the '@EntityGraph' annotation on Spring Data JPA repository methods?
options: Generates a visual diagram of database tables
Dynamically overrides lazy fetching to eagerly fetch specified entity attributes and collections in a single SQL query, resolving N+1 issues without writing custom JPQL
Maps entities to a GraphQL schema
quiz.explanation: @EntityGraph dynamically defines fetch plans, overriding lazy associations to fetch relationships in a single query via outer joins.

quiz.question: What is the difference between an embedded database (like H2) and a standalone database (like PostgreSQL) in Spring Boot?
options: An embedded database runs in-memory inside the same JVM process as the application (fast, lightweight for tests/dev, data lost upon shutdown); standalone runs as an independent external server process with persistent storage
Embedded databases do not support SQL
quiz.explanation: H2 can run entirely in-memory within the application JVM, making it ideal for unit testing and local development without installing database software.

quiz.question: What does the '@PreAuthorize("hasRole('ADMIN')")' annotation enforce?
options: Logs in the admin user automatically
Evaluates a SpEL (Spring Expression Language) security expression before method execution, blocking access with HTTP 403 Forbidden if the authenticated principal lacks the 'ROLE_ADMIN' authority
quiz.explanation: @PreAuthorize evaluates Spring Expression Language (SpEL) security rules prior to method invocation, ensuring only authenticated users with specific roles or permissions can execute the method.

quiz.question: What is Spring Boot's default embedded servlet container?
quiz.explanation: Apache Tomcat is the default embedded servlet container provided by spring-boot-starter-web. Developers can switch to Jetty or Undertow by excluding Tomcat.

quiz.question: How does Spring Boot resolve the precedence between application.properties and application.yml if both exist in the same location?
options: application.properties takes precedence and overrides properties defined in application.yml
The application fails to start with an AmbiguousConfigFileException
quiz.explanation: If both configuration files exist in the same directory, 'application.properties' takes precedence and overrides values defined in 'application.yml'.

quiz.question: What is the purpose of Spring Boot's 'spring-boot-devtools' module?
options: Provides developer productivity tools such as automatic application restart upon classpath file modification, LiveReload browser refresh, and caching disabling
Runs automated unit tests on every save
quiz.explanation: 'spring-boot-devtools' enhances local developer experience with rapid auto-restart (using two classloaders), LiveReload browser refreshing, and development-optimized property defaults.

quiz.question: What is the function of the '@ConditionalOnMissingBean' annotation in an auto-configuration class?
options: Throws an error if the bean is missing
Registers the bean only if no other bean of the same type/name has already been defined in the ApplicationContext (enabling user customization to override auto-configured defaults)
Deletes existing beans of that type
quiz.explanation: @ConditionalOnMissingBean allows Spring Boot to supply a default fallback bean while allowing developers to seamlessly override it by defining their own custom @Bean.

quiz.question: What does the 'spring.jpa.hibernate.ddl-auto=validate' property do in production?
options: Drops and recreates all database tables on every startup
Validates that the existing database schema matches the JPA entity mappings without modifying or dropping any database tables (recommended for production)
Automatically adds missing columns to tables
quiz.explanation: In production, 'validate' checks that the database schema matches entity mappings without executing DDL alterations. 'update' or 'create-drop' risk destructive data loss in production.

quiz.question: What is the purpose of database migration tools like Flyway or Liquibase in Spring Boot?
options: To convert SQL databases into MongoDB NoSQL documents
To apply version-controlled, repeatable, and automated database schema change scripts across dev, test, and production environments
To back up databases to S3 buckets
quiz.explanation: Flyway and Liquibase manage database evolution through sequential, versioned migration scripts (e.g. V1__init.sql), preventing manual schema drift between environments.

quiz.question: What does the '@ResponseStatus(HttpStatus.NOT_FOUND)' annotation on a custom exception class do?
options: Automatically translates the thrown exception into an HTTP 404 response status code sent to the client
Redirects the browser to an error page
Suppresses error logging in server logs
quiz.explanation: Annotating an exception with @ResponseStatus causes Spring MVC's ResponseStatusExceptionResolver to map the unhandled exception directly to the specified HTTP status code.

quiz.question: What is the difference between '@Component', '@Service', and '@Repository' annotations in Spring?
options: @Component is the generic stereotype for any Spring-managed component; @Service indicates business logic; @Repository indicates data access and provides automatic persistence exception translation
@Service creates prototype beans while @Component creates singletons
quiz.explanation: @Service and @Repository are specialized stereotypes of @Component. @Repository additionally catches vendor-specific database exceptions (e.g. SQLException) and translates them into Spring's DataAccessException hierarchy.

quiz.question: What is the purpose of the 'spring-boot-starter-parent' in a Maven pom.xml?
options: Provides dependency management, default compiler plugin configurations, resource filtering, and curated compatible versions for hundreds of third-party dependencies
quiz.explanation: The starter parent provides curated dependency management (eliminating version tag conflicts), sensible plugin defaults, and standardized build configurations.

quiz.question: How do you enable CORS (Cross-Origin Resource Sharing) globally in a Spring Boot application?
options: Implementing WebMvcConfigurer and overriding addCorsMappings(CorsRegistry registry)
quiz.explanation: Implementing WebMvcConfigurer and configuring addCorsMappings() sets up global CORS policies (allowed origins, methods, headers, credentials) across all endpoints cleanly.

quiz.question: What does the '@JsonIgnore' annotation on an entity field do during REST response serialization?
options: Deletes the field from the database table
Instructs Jackson to exclude the annotated property from JSON serialization and deserialization, preventing sensitive data exposure in REST responses
Validates that the field is not null
quiz.explanation: @JsonIgnore tells Jackson to ignore the field during JSON serialization and deserialization, preventing fields like password hashes from leaking in API responses.

Spring Boot Multiple Choice Questions (MCQs) - 50 Practice Questions

Assessment ⏱️ 60 min 50 Questions

Test and master your Spring Boot knowledge with this comprehensive set of 50 Multiple Choice Questions (MCQs) formatted in the classic GeeksforGeeks tutorial assessment style. Covering auto-configuration, dependency injection, REST APIs, Spring Data JPA, Hibernate N+1 resolution, transactions, security, Actuator, and microservices design.

📝 Assessment Instructions

  • Each question has four potential choices: (A), (B), (C), and (D).
  • Review the problem statement and code snippet carefully before picking your answer.
  • Click on "💡 View Answer & Explanation" to reveal the correct option along with an in-depth technical explanation.

Question 1: Which three core annotations are composed into the meta-annotation '@SpringBootApplication'?

2 Points
A) @Controller, @Service, @Repository
B) @Configuration, @EnableAutoConfiguration, @ComponentScan ✓ Correct
C) @Component, @Entity, @Bean
D) @EnableWebMvc, @EnableCaching, @Profile
💡 View Answer & Explanation

Answer: (B) @Configuration, @EnableAutoConfiguration, @ComponentScan

Explanation: @SpringBootApplication encapsulates @Configuration (declares class as a source of bean definitions), @EnableAutoConfiguration (guesses and configures beans based on classpath dependencies), and @ComponentScan (scans the current package and sub-packages for Spring components).

Question 2: What is the default bean scope in the Spring IoC Container?

2 Points
A) prototype
B) singleton ✓ Correct
C) request
D) session
💡 View Answer & Explanation

Answer: (B) singleton

Explanation: In Spring, beans are 'singleton' by default. Exactly one shared instance is instantiated and retained in the ApplicationContext cache per bean definition.

Question 3: What is the primary difference between '@Controller' and '@RestController' in Spring MVC?

2 Points
A) @RestController is only used for microservices with Eureka
B) @RestController is a convenience meta-annotation that combines @Controller and @ResponseBody, serializing returned objects directly into HTTP response bodies (JSON/XML) ✓ Correct
C) @Controller returns JSON while @RestController returns JSP views
D) There is no difference
💡 View Answer & Explanation

Answer: (B) @RestController is a convenience meta-annotation that combines @Controller and @ResponseBody, serializing returned objects directly into HTTP response bodies (JSON/XML)

Explanation: @RestController = @Controller + @ResponseBody. Every handler method in a @RestController automatically serializes domain return values into JSON/XML responses using Jackson, instead of resolving HTML view templates.

Question 4: Why is Constructor Injection strongly recommended over Field Injection (@Autowired on private fields)?

2 Points
A) Field injection requires public fields
B) Constructor injection enables fields to be declared 'final' (immutable), ensures beans cannot be initialized with null dependencies, and allows easy unit testing with mocks without reflection ✓ Correct
C) Constructor injection is faster to compile
D) Field injection was removed in Spring 5
💡 View Answer & Explanation

Answer: (B) Constructor injection enables fields to be declared 'final' (immutable), ensures beans cannot be initialized with null dependencies, and allows easy unit testing with mocks without reflection

Explanation: Constructor injection guarantees total immutability (final fields), prevents partial bean instantiation, avoids hidden circular dependencies, and enables clean POJO unit testing without needing Spring reflection containers.

Question 5: How does Spring Boot Auto-Configuration know which beans to configure?

2 Points
A) It reads all XML files in the OS file system
B) It evaluates conditional annotations like @ConditionalOnClass, @ConditionalOnMissingBean, and @ConditionalOnProperty listed in auto-configuration import files ✓ Correct
C) It queries the database schema at compile time
D) It uses AI heuristic prediction
💡 View Answer & Explanation

Answer: (B) It evaluates conditional annotations like @ConditionalOnClass, @ConditionalOnMissingBean, and @ConditionalOnProperty listed in auto-configuration import files

Explanation: Auto-configuration scans candidate classes in META-INF/spring/...AutoConfiguration.imports and evaluates condition annotations (e.g. configuring a DataSource only if DataSource.class is on classpath and no custom DataSource bean exists).

Question 6: Which Spring Boot Starter dependency is required to build RESTful web services using Apache Tomcat and Spring MVC?

2 Points
A) spring-boot-starter-tomcat-only
B) spring-boot-starter-web ✓ Correct
C) spring-boot-starter-jersey
D) spring-boot-starter-rest
💡 View Answer & Explanation

Answer: (B) spring-boot-starter-web

Explanation: 'spring-boot-starter-web' bundles Spring MVC, REST support, Jackson JSON serialization, and embedded Apache Tomcat as the default servlet container.

Question 7: What is the function of Spring Boot Actuator?

2 Points
A) Compiles Java code to native GraalVM images
B) Provides production-ready observability endpoints such as health checks (/actuator/health), metrics, thread dumps, and audit logs ✓ Correct
C) Generates database migration scripts automatically
D) Handles user JWT encryption
💡 View Answer & Explanation

Answer: (B) Provides production-ready observability endpoints such as health checks (/actuator/health), metrics, thread dumps, and audit logs

Explanation: Spring Boot Actuator brings production monitoring and management capabilities, exposing HTTP/JMX endpoints for health probes (vital for Kubernetes liveness/readiness), JVM metrics, and application info.

Question 8: What is the N+1 select problem in Spring Data JPA / Hibernate?

2 Points
A) A database deadlock error
B) An issue where fetching N parent records with lazy/eager associations triggers 1 query for the parents and N subsequent individual SQL queries for each parent's children ✓ Correct
C) A limitation preventing tables from having more than N columns
D) A primary key collision issue
💡 View Answer & Explanation

Answer: (B) An issue where fetching N parent records with lazy/eager associations triggers 1 query for the parents and N subsequent individual SQL queries for each parent's children

Explanation: The N+1 problem occurs when fetching a list of parent entities (1 query) causes Hibernate to fire a separate SQL query for each individual parent's relationship (N queries), severely degrading database performance.

Question 9: How do you solve the N+1 problem using JPQL in a Spring Data repository?

2 Points
A) Set FetchType.EAGER on the relationship
B) Use 'JOIN FETCH' in the JPQL query (e.g. 'SELECT p FROM Post p JOIN FETCH p.comments') ✓ Correct
C) Disable the second-level cache
D) Increase the database pool size
💡 View Answer & Explanation

Answer: (B) Use 'JOIN FETCH' in the JPQL query (e.g. 'SELECT p FROM Post p JOIN FETCH p.comments')

Explanation: 'JOIN FETCH' instructs Hibernate to perform an inner or left outer join in SQL, loading the parent and all associated child entities simultaneously in a single database query.

Question 10: What is the effect of applying '@Transactional' on a service class method in Spring?

2 Points
A) Logs method execution time
B) Wraps method execution within a database transaction via an AOP proxy, committing on success and rolling back on RuntimeException or Error ✓ Correct
C) Locks the thread using synchronized
D) Converts the method into an asynchronous task
💡 View Answer & Explanation

Answer: (B) Wraps method execution within a database transaction via an AOP proxy, committing on success and rolling back on RuntimeException or Error

Explanation: Spring AOP intercepts the method call, opens a database transaction, invokes the target logic, and commits if no unhandled RuntimeException occurs. By default, checked exceptions do NOT trigger a rollback unless rollbackFor is specified.

Question 11: Why does calling a '@Transactional' method from another method WITHIN THE SAME CLASS fail to start a transaction (self-invocation problem)?

2 Points
A) Transactions are prohibited on private methods
B) Spring's proxy-based AOP architecture intercepts calls entering through the proxy; direct internal method calls bypass the proxy entirely ✓ Correct
C) Internal calls cause JVM stack overflow
D) The database blocks nested method calls
💡 View Answer & Explanation

Answer: (B) Spring's proxy-based AOP architecture intercepts calls entering through the proxy; direct internal method calls bypass the proxy entirely

Explanation: Spring manages transactions via dynamic CGLIB/JDK proxies. In a self-invocation (this.method()), the call is dispatched directly on the raw target object, completely bypassing the transaction interceptor proxy.

Question 12: Which Transaction Propagation setting ensures a new, independent transaction is always created, suspending any existing transaction?

2 Points
A) Propagation.REQUIRED
B) Propagation.REQUIRES_NEW ✓ Correct
C) Propagation.NESTED
D) Propagation.SUPPORTS
💡 View Answer & Explanation

Answer: (B) Propagation.REQUIRES_NEW

Explanation: Propagation.REQUIRES_NEW suspends any current outer transaction and creates an entirely new independent physical transaction with its own commit/rollback boundaries.

Question 13: What annotation is used to create global, centralized exception handling across all @RequestMapping controllers?

2 Points
A) @GlobalErrorHandler
B) @ControllerAdvice (or @RestControllerAdvice) ✓ Correct
C) @ExceptionHandlerRegistry
D) @CatchAll
💡 View Answer & Explanation

Answer: (B) @ControllerAdvice (or @RestControllerAdvice)

Explanation: @ControllerAdvice (and @RestControllerAdvice) uses AOP to intercept exceptions thrown by any controller method, handling them with centralized @ExceptionHandler methods.

Question 14: What is the difference between '@RequestParam' and '@PathVariable'?

2 Points
A) No difference
B) '@PathVariable' extracts values directly from the URI path segment (e.g. /users/{id}); '@RequestParam' extracts query parameters from the URL query string (e.g. /users?id=123) ✓ Correct
C) '@RequestParam' is only used for POST bodies
D) '@PathVariable' requires XML format
💡 View Answer & Explanation

Answer: (B) '@PathVariable' extracts values directly from the URI path segment (e.g. /users/{id}); '@RequestParam' extracts query parameters from the URL query string (e.g. /users?id=123)

Explanation: @PathVariable binds placeholder URI path segments (/api/orders/{id}). @RequestParam binds URL query parameters (/api/orders?status=active) or form data fields.

Question 15: Which annotation binds the HTTP request body JSON directly into a Java domain object via Jackson serialization?

2 Points
A) @RequestBody ✓ Correct
B) @ResponseBody
C) @ModelAttribute
D) @EntityPayload
💡 View Answer & Explanation

Answer: (A) @RequestBody

Explanation: @RequestBody signals Spring to deserialize the incoming HTTP request body (JSON/XML) into the method parameter object using an HttpMessageConverter (such as Jackson).

Question 16: What annotation is used to bind external configuration properties from application.properties to a strongly-typed Java class?

2 Points
A) @Value
B) @ConfigurationProperties ✓ Correct
C) @PropertySource
D) @ConfigBean
💡 View Answer & Explanation

Answer: (B) @ConfigurationProperties

Explanation: @ConfigurationProperties(prefix = 'app.security') provides hierarchical, type-safe binding of configuration properties into bean fields with support for validation and IDE auto-completion.

Question 17: How does the '@Profile("production")' annotation control bean instantiation?

2 Points
A) Encrypts the bean bytecode
B) Ensures the annotated component or configuration bean is only registered in the ApplicationContext when the 'production' profile is active (spring.profiles.active=production) ✓ Correct
C) Profiles CPU execution time
D) Restricts access to admin users only
💡 View Answer & Explanation

Answer: (B) Ensures the annotated component or configuration bean is only registered in the ApplicationContext when the 'production' profile is active (spring.profiles.active=production)

Explanation: @Profile conditionally activates or deactivates beans, configurations, and properties based on active environment profiles (e.g. dev, test, prod).

Question 18: What is the role of the DispatcherServlet in Spring Boot MVC?

2 Points
A) It connects to the database via JDBC
B) It acts as the Front Controller, intercepting all incoming HTTP requests and dispatching them to the appropriate HandlerMapping, Controller, and ViewResolver ✓ Correct
C) It schedules background quartz jobs
D) It manages Tomcat thread pool threads
💡 View Answer & Explanation

Answer: (B) It acts as the Front Controller, intercepting all incoming HTTP requests and dispatching them to the appropriate HandlerMapping, Controller, and ViewResolver

Explanation: The DispatcherServlet implements the Front Controller pattern, serving as the single entry point for all HTTP requests to route them through interceptors, controllers, and message converters.

Question 19: Which method in a Spring Bean implements post-initialization logic immediately after all bean properties and dependencies have been injected?

2 Points
A) A method annotated with @PostConstruct (or implementing InitializingBean) ✓ Correct
B) A method named 'init()'
C) A method annotated with @PreDestroy
D) The class constructor
💡 View Answer & Explanation

Answer: (A) A method annotated with @PostConstruct (or implementing InitializingBean)

Explanation: The @PostConstruct annotation designates a method to be executed immediately after dependency injection is complete and before the bean is made available to callers.

Question 20: What is the difference between CrudRepository and JpaRepository in Spring Data?

2 Points
A) CrudRepository is faster than JpaRepository
B) JpaRepository extends PagingAndSortingRepository and CrudRepository, adding JPA-specific features like flush(), saveAndFlush(), batch deletions, and pagination/sorting support ✓ Correct
C) CrudRepository only works with NoSQL databases
D) JpaRepository does not support CRUD operations
💡 View Answer & Explanation

Answer: (B) JpaRepository extends PagingAndSortingRepository and CrudRepository, adding JPA-specific features like flush(), saveAndFlush(), batch deletions, and pagination/sorting support

Explanation: JpaRepository inherits CRUD and pagination/sorting capabilities from CrudRepository and PagingAndSortingRepository, adding flush() persistence context operations and deleteInBatch().

Question 21: What does the 'mappedBy' attribute signify on a bidirectional JPA relationship (e.g. @OneToMany(mappedBy = 'author'))?

2 Points
A) It maps the table name in the database
B) It identifies that the current entity is the inverse (non-owning) side of the relationship, pointing to the owning field on the target entity that manages the foreign key column ✓ Correct
C) It creates an index on the author column
D) It makes the relationship read-only
💡 View Answer & Explanation

Answer: (B) It identifies that the current entity is the inverse (non-owning) side of the relationship, pointing to the owning field on the target entity that manages the foreign key column

Explanation: 'mappedBy' designates the inverse relationship side. The side WITHOUT mappedBy is the owning side that physically holds and manages the foreign key column in SQL.

Question 22: Which Hibernate cascade type causes child entities to be automatically removed from the database when removed from the parent entity's collection?

2 Points
A) CascadeType.DETACH
B) orphanRemoval = true (alongside CascadeType.ALL) ✓ Correct
C) CascadeType.MERGE
D) CascadeType.REFRESH
💡 View Answer & Explanation

Answer: (B) orphanRemoval = true (alongside CascadeType.ALL)

Explanation: Setting 'orphanRemoval = true' instructs Hibernate to automatically delete child records from the database when they are dereferenced or removed from the parent's collection.

Question 23: What is the purpose of the '@Valid' or '@Validated' annotation on a request body parameter?

2 Points
A) Checks that the user is logged in
B) Triggers Bean Validation (Hibernate Validator) on the incoming object according to JSR-380 constraints (@NotNull, @NotBlank, @Min, @Email) ✓ Correct
C) Sanitizes HTML against XSS
D) Validates database connection health
💡 View Answer & Explanation

Answer: (B) Triggers Bean Validation (Hibernate Validator) on the incoming object according to JSR-380 constraints (@NotNull, @NotBlank, @Min, @Email)

Explanation: @Valid activates Jakarta Bean Validation. If any constraint on the payload fails, a MethodArgumentNotValidException is thrown with detailed field error results.

Question 24: What is the difference between '@NotNull', '@NotEmpty', and '@NotBlank' in Bean Validation?

2 Points
A) No difference
B) @NotNull checks value != null; @NotEmpty checks not null and length/size > 0; @NotBlank checks not null, not empty, and contains at least one non-whitespace character (strings only) ✓ Correct
C) @NotBlank can be used on lists and numbers
D) @NotNull trims whitespace automatically
💡 View Answer & Explanation

Answer: (B) @NotNull checks value != null; @NotEmpty checks not null and length/size > 0; @NotBlank checks not null, not empty, and contains at least one non-whitespace character (strings only)

Explanation: @NotNull rejects null. @NotEmpty rejects null and empty collections/strings (""). @NotBlank rejects null, empty, and strings containing only whitespace characters (" ").

Question 25: What HTTP status code is represented by 'HttpStatus.CREATED'?

2 Points
A) 200
B) 201 ✓ Correct
C) 204
D) 301
💡 View Answer & Explanation

Answer: (B) 201

Explanation: HTTP 201 Created indicates that the request succeeded and resulted in the successful creation of a new resource (standard response for POST creation endpoints).

Question 26: What HTTP status code is represented by 'HttpStatus.NO_CONTENT'?

2 Points
A) 204 ✓ Correct
B) 404
C) 200
D) 410
💡 View Answer & Explanation

Answer: (A) 204

Explanation: HTTP 204 No Content indicates that the action succeeded and no response body payload is returned (commonly returned for successful DELETE operations).

Question 27: What is the purpose of the '@Modifying' annotation in Spring Data JPA?

2 Points 
@Modifying
@Query("UPDATE User u SET u.active = false WHERE u.lastLogin < :date")
int deactivateInactiveUsers(@Param("date") LocalDate date);
A) Permits modifying table schema at runtime
B) Informs Spring Data JPA that the query is an UPDATE or DELETE DML statement rather than a SELECT query ✓ Correct
C) Enables dirty checking on returned entities
D) Forces query execution in a separate thread
💡 View Answer & Explanation

Answer: (B) Informs Spring Data JPA that the query is an UPDATE or DELETE DML statement rather than a SELECT query

Explanation: @Modifying is required on custom @Query methods that execute DML (UPDATE, DELETE, INSERT) operations, instructing the EntityManager to execute executeUpdate() instead of executeQuery().

Question 28: What is the primary role of the SecurityFilterChain bean in modern Spring Security 6+?

2 Points
A) Encrypts passwords with MD5
B) Defines the chain of security filter rules, URL authorization matchers, CSRF settings, session management, and authentication providers for HTTP requests ✓ Correct
C) Replaces database tables with LDAP
D) Generates HTTPS SSL certificates
💡 View Answer & Explanation

Answer: (B) Defines the chain of security filter rules, URL authorization matchers, CSRF settings, session management, and authentication providers for HTTP requests

Explanation: In Spring Security 5.7+ / 6+, WebSecurityConfigurerAdapter is deprecated. Developers configure a SecurityFilterChain @Bean to declare authorizeHttpRequests, OAuth2, and filters.

Question 29: Why should passwords never be stored using simple hash algorithms like MD5 or SHA-256 in Spring applications?

2 Points
A) Spring Security does not support MD5
B) They are fast computation algorithms vulnerable to brute-force and precomputed rainbow table attacks; salted adaptive key-stretching algorithms like BCrypt or Argon2 must be used ✓ Correct
C) MD5 hashes are too long for database columns
D) SHA-256 cannot hash UTF-8 text
💡 View Answer & Explanation

Answer: (B) They are fast computation algorithms vulnerable to brute-force and precomputed rainbow table attacks; salted adaptive key-stretching algorithms like BCrypt or Argon2 must be used

Explanation: MD5 and SHA-256 can compute billions of hashes per second on modern GPUs. BCrypt includes a configurable work factor and automatic salting to deliberately slow down brute-force attacks.

Question 30: What does the '@Async' annotation do when applied to a method?

2 Points
A) Makes the method synchronous
B) Runs the method in a separate background thread allocated from a ThreadPoolTaskExecutor, returning immediately to the caller (often returning CompletableFuture) ✓ Correct
C) Blocks the calling thread until completed
D) Executes the method on a web browser client
💡 View Answer & Explanation

Answer: (B) Runs the method in a separate background thread allocated from a ThreadPoolTaskExecutor, returning immediately to the caller (often returning CompletableFuture)

Explanation: @Async (coupled with @EnableAsync on configuration) executes the annotated method asynchronously in a background thread pool, allowing non-blocking execution for long tasks like email dispatch.

Question 31: What does the '@Scheduled' annotation accomplish in Spring Boot?

2 Points 
@Scheduled(cron = "0 0 12 * * ?")
public void runDailyReport() { ... }
A) Executes a method periodically at fixed intervals or based on a cron expression (requires @EnableScheduling) ✓ Correct
B) Schedules a database migration
C) Delays application startup by 12 seconds
D) Pauses garbage collection
💡 View Answer & Explanation

Answer: (A) Executes a method periodically at fixed intervals or based on a cron expression (requires @EnableScheduling)

Explanation: @Scheduled configures recurring background tasks using fixedRate, fixedDelay, or cron expressions when @EnableScheduling is active.

Question 32: What is the difference between 'fixedRate' and 'fixedDelay' in @Scheduled tasks?

2 Points
A) No difference
B) 'fixedRate' measures time between the START of successive invocations; 'fixedDelay' measures time between the FINISH of one invocation and the start of the next ✓ Correct
C) 'fixedRate' only runs on weekends
D) 'fixedDelay' cancels after one execution
💡 View Answer & Explanation

Answer: (B) 'fixedRate' measures time between the START of successive invocations; 'fixedDelay' measures time between the FINISH of one invocation and the start of the next

Explanation: 'fixedRate' starts tasks every N milliseconds regardless of execution time. 'fixedDelay' guarantees N milliseconds of idle time AFTER the preceding execution finishes.

Question 33: What is the purpose of the '@MockBean' (or '@MockitoBean' in Spring Boot 3.4+) annotation in tests?

2 Points
A) Creates a fake database table
B) Adds a Mockito mock of the bean into the Spring ApplicationContext, replacing any existing real bean of that type for integration testing ✓ Correct
C) Validates test assertions
D) Measures code coverage
💡 View Answer & Explanation

Answer: (B) Adds a Mockito mock of the bean into the Spring ApplicationContext, replacing any existing real bean of that type for integration testing

Explanation: @MockBean registers a Mockito mock inside the Spring ApplicationContext, allowing isolated testing of controllers (@WebMvcTest) with mocked service dependencies.

Question 34: What test annotation is used to test ONLY the web layer (controllers, validation, JSON serialization) without loading the full database/service context?

2 Points
A) @SpringBootTest
B) @WebMvcTest ✓ Correct
C) @DataJpaTest
D) @RestClientTest
💡 View Answer & Explanation

Answer: (B) @WebMvcTest

Explanation: @WebMvcTest focuses strictly on Spring MVC components (@Controller, @RestController, Converter), skipping @Service and @Repository beans to ensure rapid execution.

Question 35: What is the purpose of '@DataJpaTest'?

2 Points
A) Tests HTTP REST controllers
B) Configures an in-memory database, scans @Entity classes, and configures Spring Data JPA repositories within a transactional rollback test environment ✓ Correct
C) Benchmarking query speeds
D) Generates test documentation
💡 View Answer & Explanation

Answer: (B) Configures an in-memory database, scans @Entity classes, and configures Spring Data JPA repositories within a transactional rollback test environment

Explanation: @DataJpaTest focuses solely on JPA components, using an embedded in-memory database (like H2) by default and rolling back transactions at the end of each test.

Question 36: What does the 'server.servlet.context-path' property in application.properties do?

2 Points 
server.servlet.context-path=/api/v1
A) Configures the local file system path for file uploads
B) Sets the prefix path for all HTTP endpoints exposed by the embedded servlet container (e.g. localhost:8080/api/v1/...) ✓ Correct
C) Sets the database connection URL
D) Specifies the Git repository origin
💡 View Answer & Explanation

Answer: (B) Sets the prefix path for all HTTP endpoints exposed by the embedded servlet container (e.g. localhost:8080/api/v1/...)

Explanation: Setting 'server.servlet.context-path=/api/v1' prefixes all web application endpoints with '/api/v1' across the entire application.

Question 37: What is the purpose of the '@EntityGraph' annotation on Spring Data JPA repository methods?

2 Points 
@EntityGraph(attributePaths = {"items", "customer"})
List<Order> findAllWithItems();
A) Generates a visual diagram of database tables
B) Dynamically overrides lazy fetching to eagerly fetch specified entity attributes and collections in a single SQL query, resolving N+1 issues without writing custom JPQL ✓ Correct
C) Creates an index on items
D) Maps entities to a GraphQL schema
💡 View Answer & Explanation

Answer: (B) Dynamically overrides lazy fetching to eagerly fetch specified entity attributes and collections in a single SQL query, resolving N+1 issues without writing custom JPQL

Explanation: @EntityGraph dynamically defines fetch plans, overriding lazy associations to fetch relationships in a single query via outer joins.

Question 38: What is the difference between an embedded database (like H2) and a standalone database (like PostgreSQL) in Spring Boot?

2 Points
A) H2 cannot store numbers
B) An embedded database runs in-memory inside the same JVM process as the application (fast, lightweight for tests/dev, data lost upon shutdown); standalone runs as an independent external server process with persistent storage ✓ Correct
C) PostgreSQL cannot run transactions
D) Embedded databases do not support SQL
💡 View Answer & Explanation

Answer: (B) An embedded database runs in-memory inside the same JVM process as the application (fast, lightweight for tests/dev, data lost upon shutdown); standalone runs as an independent external server process with persistent storage

Explanation: H2 can run entirely in-memory within the application JVM, making it ideal for unit testing and local development without installing database software.

Question 39: What does the '@PreAuthorize("hasRole('ADMIN')")' annotation enforce?

2 Points
A) Logs in the admin user automatically
B) Evaluates a SpEL (Spring Expression Language) security expression before method execution, blocking access with HTTP 403 Forbidden if the authenticated principal lacks the 'ROLE_ADMIN' authority ✓ Correct
C) Encrypts the method return value
D) Bypasses CSRF checks
💡 View Answer & Explanation

Answer: (B) Evaluates a SpEL (Spring Expression Language) security expression before method execution, blocking access with HTTP 403 Forbidden if the authenticated principal lacks the 'ROLE_ADMIN' authority

Explanation: @PreAuthorize evaluates Spring Expression Language (SpEL) security rules prior to method invocation, ensuring only authenticated users with specific roles or permissions can execute the method.

Question 40: What is Spring Boot's default embedded servlet container?

2 Points
A) Jetty
B) Apache Tomcat ✓ Correct
C) Undertow
D) Netty
💡 View Answer & Explanation

Answer: (B) Apache Tomcat

Explanation: Apache Tomcat is the default embedded servlet container provided by spring-boot-starter-web. Developers can switch to Jetty or Undertow by excluding Tomcat.

Question 41: How does Spring Boot resolve the precedence between application.properties and application.yml if both exist in the same location?

2 Points
A) application.yml overrides application.properties
B) application.properties takes precedence and overrides properties defined in application.yml ✓ Correct
C) The application fails to start with an AmbiguousConfigFileException
D) They merge randomly
💡 View Answer & Explanation

Answer: (B) application.properties takes precedence and overrides properties defined in application.yml

Explanation: If both configuration files exist in the same directory, 'application.properties' takes precedence and overrides values defined in 'application.yml'.

Question 42: What is the purpose of Spring Boot's 'spring-boot-devtools' module?
