A) Deploys code to AWS automatically
B) Provides developer productivity tools such as automatic application restart upon classpath file modification, LiveReload browser refresh, and caching disabling ✓ Correct
C) Runs automated unit tests on every save
D) Generates Swagger UI documentation
💡 View Answer & Explanation

Answer: (B) Provides developer productivity tools such as automatic application restart upon classpath file modification, LiveReload browser refresh, and caching disabling

Explanation: 'spring-boot-devtools' enhances local developer experience with rapid auto-restart (using two classloaders), LiveReload browser refreshing, and development-optimized property defaults.

Question 43: What is the function of the '@ConditionalOnMissingBean' annotation in an auto-configuration class?

2 Points 
@Bean
@ConditionalOnMissingBean
public DataSource dataSource() { ... }
A) Throws an error if the bean is missing
B) Registers the bean only if no other bean of the same type/name has already been defined in the ApplicationContext (enabling user customization to override auto-configured defaults) ✓ Correct
C) Deletes existing beans of that type
D) Prevents bean creation entirely
💡 View Answer & Explanation

Answer: (B) Registers the bean only if no other bean of the same type/name has already been defined in the ApplicationContext (enabling user customization to override auto-configured defaults)

Explanation: @ConditionalOnMissingBean allows Spring Boot to supply a default fallback bean while allowing developers to seamlessly override it by defining their own custom @Bean.

Question 44: What does the 'spring.jpa.hibernate.ddl-auto=validate' property do in production?

2 Points
A) Drops and recreates all database tables on every startup
B) Validates that the existing database schema matches the JPA entity mappings without modifying or dropping any database tables (recommended for production) ✓ Correct
C) Automatically adds missing columns to tables
D) Validates user passwords
💡 View Answer & Explanation

Answer: (B) Validates that the existing database schema matches the JPA entity mappings without modifying or dropping any database tables (recommended for production)

Explanation: In production, 'validate' checks that the database schema matches entity mappings without executing DDL alterations. 'update' or 'create-drop' risk destructive data loss in production.

Question 45: What is the purpose of database migration tools like Flyway or Liquibase in Spring Boot?

2 Points
A) To convert SQL databases into MongoDB NoSQL documents
B) To apply version-controlled, repeatable, and automated database schema change scripts across dev, test, and production environments ✓ Correct
C) To benchmark database query latency
D) To back up databases to S3 buckets
💡 View Answer & Explanation

Answer: (B) To apply version-controlled, repeatable, and automated database schema change scripts across dev, test, and production environments

Explanation: Flyway and Liquibase manage database evolution through sequential, versioned migration scripts (e.g. V1__init.sql), preventing manual schema drift between environments.

Question 46: What does the '@ResponseStatus(HttpStatus.NOT_FOUND)' annotation on a custom exception class do?

public class ResourceNotFoundException extends RuntimeException { ... }

B) Automatically translates the thrown exception into an HTTP 404 response status code sent to the client ✓ Correct

D) Suppresses error logging in server logs
💡 View Answer & Explanation

Answer: (B) Automatically translates the thrown exception into an HTTP 404 response status code sent to the client

Explanation: Annotating an exception with @ResponseStatus causes Spring MVC's ResponseStatusExceptionResolver to map the unhandled exception directly to the specified HTTP status code.

Question 47: What is the difference between '@Component', '@Service', and '@Repository' annotations in Spring?

2 Points
A) They have completely different lifecycles
B) @Component is the generic stereotype for any Spring-managed component; @Service indicates business logic; @Repository indicates data access and provides automatic persistence exception translation ✓ Correct
C) @Repository cannot be injected into services
D) @Service creates prototype beans while @Component creates singletons
💡 View Answer & Explanation

Answer: (B) @Component is the generic stereotype for any Spring-managed component; @Service indicates business logic; @Repository indicates data access and provides automatic persistence exception translation

Explanation: @Service and @Repository are specialized stereotypes of @Component. @Repository additionally catches vendor-specific database exceptions (e.g. SQLException) and translates them into Spring's DataAccessException hierarchy.

Question 48: What is the purpose of the 'spring-boot-starter-parent' in a Maven pom.xml?

2 Points
A) Downloads the JDK compiler
B) Provides dependency management, default compiler plugin configurations, resource filtering, and curated compatible versions for hundreds of third-party dependencies ✓ Correct
C) Enforces Java 8 compatibility only
D) Connects to Oracle Maven repositories
💡 View Answer & Explanation

Answer: (B) Provides dependency management, default compiler plugin configurations, resource filtering, and curated compatible versions for hundreds of third-party dependencies

Explanation: The starter parent provides curated dependency management (eliminating version tag conflicts), sensible plugin defaults, and standardized build configurations.

Question 49: How do you enable CORS (Cross-Origin Resource Sharing) globally in a Spring Boot application?

2 Points
A) Disabling the firewall
B) Implementing WebMvcConfigurer and overriding addCorsMappings(CorsRegistry registry) ✓ Correct
C) Adding @CrossOrigin on every Java class
D) Setting server.cors.enabled=true
💡 View Answer & Explanation

Answer: (B) Implementing WebMvcConfigurer and overriding addCorsMappings(CorsRegistry registry)

Explanation: Implementing WebMvcConfigurer and configuring addCorsMappings() sets up global CORS policies (allowed origins, methods, headers, credentials) across all endpoints cleanly.

Question 50: What does the '@JsonIgnore' annotation on an entity field do during REST response serialization?

2 Points 
@JsonIgnore
private String passwordHash;
A) Deletes the field from the database table
B) Instructs Jackson to exclude the annotated property from JSON serialization and deserialization, preventing sensitive data exposure in REST responses ✓ Correct
C) Encrypts the field with AES
D) Validates that the field is not null

Answer: (B) Instructs Jackson to exclude the annotated property from JSON serialization and deserialization, preventing sensitive data exposure in REST responses

Spring Boot Interview Questions & Answers

Interview Preparation ⏱️ 20 min read

Curated technical interview questions covering foundational principles, edge cases, and high-level architectural patterns frequently encountered in Spring Boot developer interviews.

Q1: How does Spring Boot Auto-Configuration work?

Easy
📖 View Technical Answer & Deep-Dive
Spring Boot auto-configuration attempts to automatically configure your Spring application based on jar dependencies added to the classpath.

Mechanics:
  • When @EnableAutoConfiguration is active, Spring scans META-INF/spring/org.springframework.boot.autoconfigure.AutoConfiguration.imports (or spring.factories in older versions).
  • It checks conditions using annotations like @ConditionalOnClass, @ConditionalOnMissingBean, and @ConditionalOnProperty.
  • If conditions are satisfied (e.g. H2Dialect and DataSource on classpath and no custom DataSource defined), it auto-registers the appropriate beans.

Q2: Explain Spring Bean Scopes.

Medium
📖 View Technical Answer & Deep-Dive
Spring supports six bean scopes (four available only in web-aware contexts):
  • singleton (Default): Scopes a single bean definition to a single object instance per Spring IoC container.
  • prototype: Creates a brand new bean instance every single time a request for that bean is made.
  • request: Scopes a bean instance to an HTTP request lifecycle.
  • session: Scopes a bean instance to an HTTP Session lifecycle.
  • application: Scopes a bean instance to the lifecycle of a ServletContext.
  • websocket: Scopes a bean instance to the lifecycle of a WebSocket.

Q3: What is the N+1 problem in Hibernate / Spring Data JPA and how is it resolved?

Medium
📖 View Technical Answer & Deep-Dive
The N+1 problem happens when fetching a list of parent entities (1 query) causes Hibernate to execute an additional individual query for each parent's associated children (N queries), resulting in N+1 database queries.

Solutions:
  • JOIN FETCH: Use JPQL SELECT p FROM Post p JOIN FETCH p.comments to load parents and children in a single SQL query.
  • @EntityGraph: Annotate repository query methods with @EntityGraph(attributePaths = {'comments'}) to declare eager fetch paths.
  • Batch Size: Configure spring.jpa.properties.hibernate.default_batch_fetch_size=20 to batch queries using SQL IN (...) clauses.

Q4: How does @Transactional work in Spring?

Hard
📖 View Technical Answer & Deep-Dive
@Transactional leverages Spring AOP (Aspect-Oriented Programming) to manage database transactions declaratively.

Mechanism:
  • Spring generates a dynamic proxy around the target bean.
  • When a method is called, the transaction interceptor opens a transaction via the PlatformTransactionManager.
  • If the method completes successfully, the transaction is committed.
  • By default, transactions are automatically rolled back on RuntimeException and Error, but NOT on checked exceptions unless configured via @Transactional(rollbackFor = Exception.class).
  • Self-invocation (calling a transactional method from within the same class) bypasses the proxy, causing the transaction to NOT activate!
